findings.desc: quantum_claim_check only applies the requestedStrength CLI argument to built-in cases. In packages/main/src/handlers/quantum-claim-admissibility.ts:108-110 the handler skips args.requestedStrength whenever evidenceJson or evidencePath is present, even though the command schema exposes requestedStrength as a normal argument and describes unsupported strengths as fail-closed overclaims. As a result, caller-supplied complete evidence plus --requestedStrength=production/theory can be evaluated as advance unless the JSON itself redundantly includes requestedStrength, creating CLI/direct-input policy drift and a fail-closed overclaim bypass. Apply requestedStrength consistently after parsing all evidence sources, or reject combining it with evidenceJson/evidencePath so the command cannot silently ignore the overclaim signal.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commits 4803d15f5 and e896ad5d9: requestedStrength now applies after all evidence parsing, including evidenceJson/evidencePath, and real CLI inline JSON no longer fails schema validation. Verified by build, quantum smoke, command-catalog smoke, command-ownership contract, and exact CLI repro returning decision=stop for evidenceJson + requestedStrength=production.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/claim-admissibility-adapter-pack-framework.md says the M2/default registry includes the Quantum local gate-policy projection (lines 292-313), but the actual default Quantum pack remains descriptor/normalization-only with gatePolicies: Object.freeze([]) in packages/main/src/core/claim-admissibility/pack-framework.ts. The M3 projection is registered separately as the quantum_claim_check CLI handler, so the doc can falsely imply the generic adapter framework M4 Gate Policy Adapter is complete. Reword to keep the pack registry at descriptor/normalization only, describe quantum_claim_check as a separate local M3 projection, and update the stale Open Design Question reference to beyond M3 or equivalent.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 4803d15f5: framework docs now state the Quantum pack remains descriptor/normalization-only with empty gatePolicies; Quantum M3 local projection is separate through quantum_claim_check, and generic framework M4 gatePolicies remains future work.

findings.desc: quantum_claim_check exposes requestedStrength as a normal fail-closed overclaim control, including production/theory/hardware/Authority strengths, but the handler only applies args.requestedStrength when no evidenceJson or evidencePath is supplied. A caller can provide otherwise complete custom evidence and pass --requestedStrength=production or --requestedStrength=theory; because packages/main/src/handlers/quantum-claim-admissibility.ts skips the override for custom evidence, evaluateQuantumClaimGatePolicy can see a scoped request and return decision=advance instead of stop. This makes the local gate-policy decision less meaningful for direct evidence input and creates a production/theory overclaim bypass at the CLI boundary. Apply requestedStrength consistently after parsing all evidence sources, or reject combining requestedStrength with evidenceJson/evidencePath so unsupported strengths cannot be silently ignored.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commits 4803d15f5 and e896ad5d9: same root cause as F-001; custom evidence plus requestedStrength production/theory/hardware overclaims are no longer ignored and fail closed instead of advancing.

findings.desc: Test coverage misses the direct evidence input path for quantum_claim_check. The focused smoke covers built-in complete/degraded/stale/missing/mismatched/unbound/overclaim cases and direct handler productionDone rejection, but it never exercises evidenceJson/evidencePath combined with requestedStrength. The actual CLI path rejects JSON object evidence before the handler because command-catalog declares evidenceJson as string while the flag parser supplies an object; when the handler is called directly with evidenceJson as a string plus requestedStrength=production, it returns decision=advance with no reasons. Add coverage for evidenceJson/evidencePath direct-input parsing and requestedStrength overclaim precedence so the advertised direct evidence CLI path fails closed instead of remaining untested.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commits 4803d15f5 and e896ad5d9: smoke coverage now includes direct evidenceJson/evidencePath with requestedStrength=production, and command-catalog smoke verifies CLI schema accepts inline JSON while preserving fail-closed stop behavior.
